source: Original (freshly authored, calculator allowed). Introduction to geometric sequences: 4, 12, 36, 108, ...; ratios and r, u_n, u_10, smallest n with u_n > 1 000 000.

parts.label: a
parts.description: For the geometric sequence 4, 12, 36, 108, ..., find u_2/u_1, u_3/u_2 and u_4/u_3. Hence write down the common ratio r.
parts.tolerance: Accept the ratios written as fractions or as the value 3.
parts.notes: M1 for at least two of the three ratios correctly calculated. A1 for r = 3. A common difference in place of a ratio (e.g. 12 - 4 = 8) earns no marks.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Write down an expression for u_n in terms of n, given u_n = u_1 r^(n-1).
parts.notes: A1 for 4 * 3^(n-1) or an equivalent form. u_n = 4 * 3^n or 12^(n-1) earns no mark.
parts.follow_through: Award A1 for 4 * r^(n-1) with the candidate's own r from (a).

parts.label: c
parts.tolerance: Accept 78732 obtained by any method, including a GDC sequence table or repeated multiplication by 3.
parts.notes: A1 for 78732. Using 3^10 (giving 236196) earns no mark unless it follows from the candidate's own expression in (b).
parts.follow_through: Award A1 for the value obtained by substituting n = 10 into the candidate's own expression from (b).

parts.label: d
parts.description: Find the smallest value of n for which u_n > 1 000 000.
parts.tolerance: Accept any valid method: an inequality 4 * 3^(n-1) > 1000000 solved on the GDC or with logarithms (n - 1 > 11.31..., so n = 13), or a table search. For a table search, full marks for the adjacent rows u_12 = 708588 and u_13 = 2125764 with n = 13 stated; a single row (u_13 = 2125764, so n = 13) also earns full marks.
parts.notes: M1 for setting up the inequality (or equation) with the u_n expression and 1 000 000, or for a table/list of terms reaching past 1 000 000. A1 for n = 13. A non-integer final answer (12.31...) earns the M1 only; rounding down to n = 12 earns the M1 only. On a single-row table search, attach the feedback note that the adjacent row u_12 is what justifies 'smallest' (markscheme-spec section 18).
parts.follow_through: Award A1 for the smallest integer n correctly obtained from the candidate's own expression in (b).

source: Original (freshly authored, calculator allowed). Town population 12 000 at start of 2020 growing 4% per year; car bought for $24 000 at start of 2020 depreciating 15% per year.

parts.label: a
parts.description: The population of a town was 12 000 at the start of 2020 and increases by 4% each year. Write down the common ratio of the geometric sequence formed by the population at the start of each year.
parts.notes: A1 for r = 1.04. r = 0.04 or r = 4 earns no mark.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Find the population at the start of 2030.
parts.tolerance: Accept any value that rounds to 17760, including 17800 (3 s.f.), 17762, 17762.9 and 17763. Accept the term-number route u_11 = 12000 * 1.04^10, which is the same calculation.
parts.notes: M1 for 12000 multiplied by the growth multiplier raised to the power 10 (ten years of growth), however written, including repeated multiplication on the GDC. A1 for 17763 or an accepted rounding. An exponent of 9 (17079.7...) or 11 (18473.4...) earns the M1 only.
parts.follow_through: Award M1A1 for 12000 * r^10 evaluated with the candidate's own r from (a), provided r > 1.

parts.label: c
parts.description: A car was bought for $24 000 at the start of 2020 and its value decreases by 15% each year. Find the value of the car after 5 years.
parts.tolerance: Accept any value that rounds to $10600 at 3 s.f., including $10649 and $10648.93.
parts.notes: M1 for a multiplier of 0.85 applied five times to 24000, however written. A1 for 10648.93 or an accepted rounding. A multiplier of 0.15 (giving $1.82) or 1.15 earns no marks. An exponent of 4 ($12528.15) earns the M1 only.

parts.label: d
parts.description: Find the number of complete years after which the value of the car first falls below $5000.
parts.tolerance: Accept any valid method: an inequality 24000 * 0.85^n < 5000 solved on the GDC or with logarithms (n > 9.65..., so 10), or a table search. For a table search, full marks for the adjacent years (9 years: $5558.81; 10 years: $4724.99) with 10 stated; a single row (after 10 years the value is $4724.99, so 10) also earns full marks.
parts.notes: M1 for setting up the inequality (or equation) with 24000, the 0.85 multiplier and 5000, or for a table/list of yearly values reaching below 5000. A1 for 10 years. A non-integer final answer (9.65) earns the M1 only; rounding down to 9 earns the M1 only. On a single-row table search, attach the feedback note that the adjacent year 9 is what justifies 'first' (markscheme-spec section 18).
parts.follow_through: Award A1 for the smallest whole number of years correctly obtained from the candidate's own multiplier in (c), provided it is between 0 and 1.
